Nebraska site selection. Phelps County was selected because it combines substantial corn and soybean production with extensive center-pivot irrigation (USDA Census of Agriculture and NRCS irrigation data). The sampled farm includes pivot-shaped fields alongside rectangular quarters, so the shape and crop-history comparisons include irrigated and dryland patterns.
All figures and tables in this page are generated from real grower field boundaries in the runtime data root. The analysis is read-only and does not download data.

Key findings

  • Scope. 30 fields across 3 states (IL, IA, NE) and 3 growers, with weather and CDL history for 2021-2025.
  • Field geometry. IA (Iowa) median 147 ac (n=10); IL (Illinois) median 76 ac (n=10); NE (Nebraska) median 127 ac (n=10). Shape mix: IA: 80% rectangular, 0% pivot-like, 20% irregular; IL: 20% rectangular, 0% pivot-like, 80% irregular; NE: 20% rectangular, 40% pivot-like, 40% irregular.
  • Weather. Median growing-season totals across years: IA (Iowa) 542 mm and 1713 GDD; IL (Illinois) 592 mm and 1964 GDD; NE (Nebraska) 467 mm and 2062 GDD. Fields inside a farm share a NASA POWER cell, so B3 puts same-farm pairs at rho close to 1.0 and the useful signal is the between-state gradient.
  • Crop history. IA: 60% corn-years, 40% soybean-years, 10% continuous corn; IL: 48% corn-years, 52% soybean-years, 0% continuous corn; NE: 68% corn-years, 22% soybean-years, 20% continuous corn.
  • Latest crop mix. IA (Iowa) 2025: 43% corn / 55% soybean; IL (Illinois) 2025: 50% corn / 50% soybean; NE (Nebraska) 2025: 76% corn / 21% soybean.
  • Boundary vs CDL. NE osm-1353292294 (OOOOO) is tagged as farmland in OpenStreetMap but CDL reports mostly non-crop cover. It is kept as Other instead of silently dropped, so the crop statistics show the disagreement between the boundary source and the satellite classification.
  • Interpretation. These are descriptive comparisons of real field boundaries and public data. They do not establish causal effects, and field-level CDL mixes can include non-crop pixels at edges.

Methods

  • Boundaries. Areas, perimeters, and shapes are computed in an equal-area projected CRS (EPSG:5070). Polsby-Popper compactness is 4πA/P²; rectangle fill is polygon area divided by minimum rotated rectangle area.
  • Weather. Daily NASA POWER series are sampled at each field centroid. Growing degree days use base 10 °C and a 30 °C upper cap. The growing season is April-October; frost dates use daily minimum temperature ≤ 0 °C.
  • Crop history. USDA CDL pixels are summarised per field-year and collapsed to a dominant crop. Rotation diversity is the Shannon entropy of a field's mean crop shares; transitions count year-to-year dominant-crop changes.
  • Statistics. Correlations are Spearman rho with permutation p-values; group medians are descriptive and not adjusted for multiple comparisons.

Reproducibility

The analysis is reproducible from the committed scripts and the runtime data root:

python scripts/eda/eda_field_level.py --command all \
  --grower illinois-grower --grower iowa-grower --grower nebraska-grower \
  --start-year 2021 --end-year 2025 \
  --cdl-years 2021,2022,2023,2024,2025 --seed 2026

python scripts/reporting/generate_eda_report.py --eda-dir /home/coder/my-farm-advisor-runtime/data-pipeline/shared/eda/field-level

Boundary input SHA-256 values are recorded in manifest.json, along with every generated table and figure path.

Run seed: 2026. Weather rows: 54780; CDL rows: 329.

Limitations

  • Field boundaries come from OpenStreetMap and are not legal survey boundaries.
  • CDL is a 30 m classification; field edges mix crops, roads, and non-crop pixels.
  • NASA POWER grid cells are coarser than fields, so nearby fields can share weather values.
  • Because every field in a farm falls inside one NASA POWER cell, within-farm temperature correlations are effectively 1.0 by construction; B3 therefore measures the gradient between states, not within-farm microclimate.
  • Ten fields per state support descriptive comparison, not statewide inference.
  • This report contains no soil analysis and no interactive dashboard, by design.
